title: 30 vs 144 Hz determinism checks are blind to frame-rate dependence (and cost 318 s)
detail: Both the Node test (tests/unit/sim/bots.test.ts:63) and the e2e drive bots that read the sim every tick, so input is tick-quantized and the log can't depend on frame rate whatever the loop does. Proof: a scratch loop that runs exactly ONE tick per frame regardless of dt (game 4.8x slower at 30 Hz: 97.4 s vs 20.3 s wall) still gives identical logs at 30 and 144 Hz for seeds 7/12345/42 (scratch det.test.ts, passed). SC1/exceptional #8 are therefore unproven by these tests; only loop.test.ts covers tick counts. The e2e also renders every one of ~14k frames for 6 runs, which is why it takes 318 s of an 11m48s verify. Fix: (a) assert wall time to result (frames*dt) equals result.tick/120 within one frame at both rates; (b) drive input through __lily.press at wall times on the common 166.67 ms grid (5 frames @30, 24 @144, 20 ticks) instead of bots, so the shell pending->tick path is exercised; (c) cut the browser run to one seed and draw only every Nth frame (CEO-approved hook option, e.g. frame(dt,n,{draw:false})) since Node already covers 200 seeds. Target < 30 s.

title: In-browser sim-step p95 budget check is vacuous (coarse timer reads 0)
detail: lastSimStepMs is a performance.now() delta around one ~µs step (shell.ts:257,266); Chromium's clamped timer returns 0, so p95 <= 0.25 always passes (WO-002 report: 'lastSimStepMs is 0.000'). It is reported as a budget check but cannot fail. Fix: time a batch (e.g. 1200 steps of a cloned run) inside page.evaluate and divide, or delete the check and cite the Node budget test as the only evidence.

title: Tap-on-pad during the 40 ms retarget window retargets the current hop to a different pad
detail: While squashing, sim.choices is empty, so tapCandidates() offers the layer AFTER the hop target and slotOf() maps a tapped k+2 pad via positionalSlot. If that tap is consumed within ticks(40)=5 of hop start, sim.ts:344 treats it as a retarget and redirects the CURRENT hop in layer k+1 (e.g. fast double-tap L-pad then R-pad ahead: frog veers right, possibly onto a soggy/curl or flanked pad). Conversely a tap on another pad in the target layer during that window isn't a candidate and falls to screen thirds. Fix: in tapCandidates, while frog.phase==='squash' && tick-hopTick<=retarget ticks, return the target layer's pads (from the takeoff pad) so the tap retargets to the pad actually tapped; only offer the layer after the target once retarget is closed.

title: Flanked X chip vanishes during squash but a retarget can still land on the armed flank
detail: startHop -> refreshChoices sets choices=[] and resets the flanked pad to idle, yet handlePress (sim.ts:344-351) lets a different key within 5 ticks retarget onto the armed flank pad, which is then judged eaten at land (sim.ts:261). The deadly pad loses its tell for the exact window in which it can still be chosen. Fix: in refreshChoices keep an armed flank pad 'flanked' while the frog is in squash, or make retarget refuse an armed flank pad (treat as a dropped press).

title: Pause-button e2e silently passes if the button is missing
detail: if (await btn.count()) ... else console.log('note ...') was a pre-WO-003 crutch; the button now exists (ui.ts:74 data-test=pause) so the branch is dead, but a renamed selector would turn the check into a note. Fix: check(await btn.count() === 1, 'pause button present') and drop the else.

title: Small per-frame allocations in the frame path
detail: view() builds a new ViewState every render; renderer.ts:690 (isChoice) and :862 (particles callback) allocate closures per frame; input.ts:196 allocates a PadMemory per connected gamepad per poll. Heap growth is within budget (look-perf +0.26 MB), so taste-level. Fix: reuse one mutable ViewState and PadMemory per slot; hoist the two closures to createRenderer scope reading a captured sim ref.

It has no shadow, cuts hard vertical edges through both banks at x=290/1150, and its torn bottom reads like a waterline. The pads under it turn pale, so the first frame shows a new 'ghost' pad look in a game about spotting look-alike pads. It also breaks the cut-paper rule (§5.2: hard ink shadow). Should be: remove the full-width sheet. Either (a) set the wordmark straight on the pond per §7.1 (ink, 3 px paper offset, plus a 4 px ink shadow at 38%), or (b) use a small opaque torn paper label (wordmark + 24 px padding, tilt -2°, 6 px hard ink shadow, like the cards) that covers no pad by more than 10%. Never tint the pads. sim.ts refreshChoices no longer resets 'flanked'; arming sets the pad flanked unconditionally; only clearFlank or an eaten-still lunge clears it. New test gator.test.ts 'F-004': armed pad stays flanked through squash+air while a retarget lands on it -> eaten cause flank; plus 'eaten standing still releases an armed flank pad'. npx vitest run tests/unit/sim: 47/47.

Root cause: a pad tap was mapped to a slot at tap time against the wrong layer, and taps on near-future pads fell through to screen thirds. Now shell.ts holds the tapped pad (pendingPad) and maps it only on the consuming tick, via pressLayer() (retarget window → target layer, else target+1). A pad not reachable on that tick is dropped, never sent elsewhere. While airborne, both the target layer and the next are tap candidates, so they never fall to thirds. Proof: tests/unit/app/shell.test.ts 'tap timing against the real sim' has 4 tests, including a sweep over 3 first pads × 33 tap ticks × 6 second pads asserting landings ⊆ {first, tapped}. With HEAD's shell.ts swapped in, all 3 tap tests fail; with the fix, 14/14 pass (15/15 reruns green).

title: Wide-screen win zoom has no floor (~0.13x at 1440x900), contradicting 7.5's 0.4x; frame is mostly sand
detail: The F-012 fix fits the whole route on w >= 1024: k=(900-136)/982 wu = 0.78 px/wu, zoom = k/6 = 0.13. Spec 7.5 step 4 says ease out to 0.4x 'if it fits'. Result (artifacts/shots/look-11-win-desktop.jpg, 2026-11-21): an ~80 px river strip in ~1440 px of sand, pads ~16 px, which is F-012's 'mostly empty sand' complaint in a new form. Fix: clamp zoom to the 0.4x floor on wide screens as well (show the latest ~2/5 of the route and let the trace scroll), or get a designer ruling that amends 7.5 and recomposes the frame (e.g. card beside a centred, larger river).
